boundary_condition: Apply only to hotel lodging searches where a multi-room stay is relevant; do not apply to solo/couple stays or to non-hotel travel tasks.
condition: When making a hotel booking for a group/family or other stay needing multiple sleeping spaces, and no different room count is specified.
exception_condition: If the user explicitly specifies a different room count, or a bed/occupancy setup that requires more or fewer than two rooms, follow that explicit requirement instead of defaulting to two rooms.
name: Default to two rooms for group hotel stays
rationale: Several independent hotel task dialogues explicitly request two rooms, while the accompanying bed and party details vary and are therefore treated as transaction-specific rather than part of the habit. This supports a controlled synthetic default of asking for two rooms only within multi-room hotel-booking contexts.

source_evidence.contribution: The user states, "I want two rooms," directly supporting a two-room hotel-room-count preference.
The user says they will need "two rooms next to each other" for a hotel stay, supporting a two-room default in group lodging contexts.
The user plainly says, "I need two rooms," giving direct evidence for requesting two hotel rooms.
The user says, "We want two rooms," with bed details for each room, supporting the reusable room-count value while leaving bed setup as request-specific.

source_examples.user_utterance: Amenities, yes. They have to all have coffee makers and refrigerators, which they probably will, but two rooms need to have king-size beds and the other one needs to have a queen and a twin or two queens.
Yeah, I want two rooms with four-person and three kids.
Well, First off, There will be four of us, So we'll need two rooms next to each other.
We want two rooms. One room has a queen and the other has two twins.
